💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re self-employed and can’t join a spouse’s job-based strategy, buy health insurance through HealthCare.gov or your state’s Marketplace, where the premium tax credit depends on your expected net income for the coverage year.
  • It has been revealed that price a spouse’s job-based plan first, since being able to join one usually rules out the credit and the deduction.
  • It has been revealed that otherwise, the credit is based on the net income you expect for the coverage year, and your tax return checks it against what you earned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re self-employed and can’t join a spouse’s job-based strategy, buy health insurance through HealthCare.gov or your state’s Marketplace, where the premium tax credit depends on your expected net income for the coverage year. Deduct the premiums you pay, and update your estimate as income changes, since you now repay any excess credit in full.

It has been revealed that price a spouse’s job-based plan first, since being able to join one usually rules out the credit and the deduction. Workers with job-based family coverage pay about 27% of the premium on average, KFF’s 2026 Employer Health Benefits Survey found.

It has been revealed that otherwise, the credit is based on the net income you expect for the coverage year, and your tax return checks it against what you earned. Starting with tax year 2026, the IRS makes you repay any excess credit in full. Household income above 400% of the federal poverty level gets no credit, so ending the year above that line means repaying every dollar of credit you received.

Build the estimate from the profit you expect after business expenses, and update it on HealthCare.gov or your state’s Marketplace as soon as your expected profit changes. A freelance designer projecting $45,000 of net income buys a plan with the credit. When a major client signs in June, she raises her estimate that week, which cuts her monthly credit now instead of leaving an excess to repay. Near the 400% line, take only part of the credit in advance and claim the rest you qualify for when you file.

A lean year can qualify you for Medicaid, which the same application checks. A professional association or freelancers group may offer a strategy too, but the credit applies only to Marketplace prepares. Outside the Marketplace, short-term plans may not cover a condition you already have. Medical discount plans and health care sharing ministries, which pool members’ money for one another’s bills, aren’t insurance at all, the National Association of Insurance Commissioners warns.

At tax time, deduct the part of the premium the credit didn’t cover, as long as the business made a profit. Since 2026, a bronze proposal, the tier with the highest deductibles, also lets you save pretax money in a health savings account (HSA).

Each time you pay quarterly estimated taxes, compare your profit so far with the income on your Marketplace application, and update the estimate that day.

College students have a lot on their plate already, including the need to study to get good grades, participating in any number of on-campus activities and potentially working part-time to have some spending money.

That noted, college students should also focus on their financial future, including steps they can take to build credit before they enter the workforce.

After all, having a credit history and a good credit score can mean being able to rent an apartment, finance a car or take out a loan, whereas having no credit at all can mean sitting on the sidelines until the situation changes.

In a recent development, fortunately, there are all kinds of ways for young adults to build credit while they’re still in school. Some strategies require a little work on their part, but many are hands-off tasks that you only have to do once.

Make sure your student knows the basic cornerstones of credit building, including the factors that are used to determine credit scores. While factors like fresh credit, length of credit history and credit mix will play a role in their credit later on, the two most important concerns for credit newcomers to focus on include payment history and credit utilization.

Payment history makes up 35% of FICO scores and credit utilization ratio makes up 30% of scores.

In a recent development, generally speaking, college students and everyone else can score well in these categories by making all bill payments on time and keeping debt levels low. How low?

Most experts recommend keeping credit utilization below 30% at a maximum and below 10% for the best possible results. This means trying to owe less than $300 for every $1,000 in available credit limits at a maximum, but preferably less than $100 for every $1,000 in credit limits.

Recent findings suggest that one step you can personally take to help a child build credit is adding them to your credit card account as an authorized user. This means they will get a credit card in their name and access to your spending limit, but you are legally responsible for any charges they make. Obviously, this move works best when you have excellent credit and a strong history of on-time payments and you plan to continue using credit responsibly .

While this step can be risky if you’re worried your college student will use their card to overspend, you don’t actually have to give them their physical authorized user credit card.

Industry observers note that in fact, they can get credit for your on-time payments whether they have access to a card or not. If you do decide to give them their credit card, you can do so with the agreement they can only use it for emergency expenses.

Your child can build credit faster if they apply for a credit card and get approved for one on their own, yet this can be difficult for students who have no credit history. That stated, secured credit cards require a refundable cash deposit as collateral are very easy to get approved for.

Industry observers note that some secured credit cards like the Ambition Card by College Ave even offer cash back1 on every purchase and don’t charge interest2. If your child opts to start building credit with a secured credit card, make sure they understand the best ways to build credit quickly — keeping credit utilization low and paying bills early or on time each month.

While secured credit cards are a good option for students with little to no credit get started on their journey to good credit, there are also credit cards specifically designed for college students. Student credit cards are unsecured cards, meaning they don’t require an upfront cash deposit as collateral, but charge interest on any purchases not paid in full each month.

In a recent development, many student credit cards offer rewards for spending with no annual fee required as well, although these cards do tend to come with a high APR. The key to getting the most out of a student credit card is having your dependent use it only for purchases they can afford and paying off the balance in its entirety each billing cycle. After all, sky high interest rates don’t really matter when you never carry a balance from one month to the next.

“One of the safest ways for college student to build their credit by learning valuable money skills.”.

While secured cards and student credit cards help young adults build credit with each bill payment they make, other payments they’re making can also help.

In fact, using an app like Experian Boost can help them get credit for utility bills they’re paying, subscriptions they pay for and even rent payments they’re making. This app is also free to use, and you only have to set up most bill payments in the app once to have them reported to the credit bureaus.

There are also rent-specific apps and tools students can use to get credit for rent payments, although they come with fees. Examples include websites like Rental Kharma and RentReporters.

The Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) also notes that students can start building credit with their student loans during school, even if they’re not officially required to make payments until six months after graduation with federal student loans.

Their advice is to make interest-only payments on federal student loans along with payments on any private student loans they have during college in order to start having those payments reported to the credit bureaus as soon as possible.

“Making interest-only payments as a student will not only positively affect your credit history but will also keep the interest from capitalizing and adding to your student loan balance,” the agency writes.

It has been revealed that of course, interest capitalization on loans would only be an problem with private student loans and  Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans since the U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on Direct Subsidized Loans while you’re in school at least half-time, for six months after you graduate and during periods of deferment.

Industry observers note that college students don’t have to wait until they’re done with school to start building credit for the future, and it makes sense to start building positive credit habits early on regardless. Tools like a credit card can help students on their way, whether they opt for a secured credit card or a student card. Other steps like using credit-building apps can also help, and with little effort on the student’s part or on yours.

In a recent development, either way, the best time to start building credit was a few years ago, and the second best time is now. You can give your student a leg up on the future by helping them build credit so it’s there when they need it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Once a lodger lives down the hall, a bad match is hard to undo, and your state’s law decides how hard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A lodger in your spare room can cover a big share of your mortgage. Before anyone moves in, confirm that zoning and your homeowners association allow it, and learn how your state lets you end the arrangement. Then screen the lodger, sign a written room agreement, and deduct the room’s share of costs from the rent you report.

Once a lodger lives down the hall, a bad match is hard to undo, and your state’s law decides how hard.

It has been revealed that california’s courts spell out a simpler way to end it. The rule covers a single lodger in a house you live in, as long as you keep the right to enter their room. Written notice giving them one rental period to leave, such as a month for monthly rent, ends their right to stay, and police may remove a lodger who stays past it. Rent to two people and the rule no longer applies, so ending it takes a court eviction.

Local zoning can cap how many unrelated people share a house, and a homeowners association’s rules may restrict rentals. If you rent, get your landlord’s written consent.

Check an applicant’s credit and eviction records with their written consent, verify their income, and call a past landlord. Then sign a room agreement that covers the rent, deposit, shared spaces, utilities, guests, quiet hours, and notice to leave. Before move-in, tell your insurer you’re taking in a lodger, and have the lodger buy renters insurance.

Sources indicate that under IRS Publication 527, the rent is taxable income, usually reported on Schedule E, the form for rental income. Only a home rented out 14 days a year or less escapes that tax. You split shared costs like mortgage interest, property tax, utilities, and insurance by number of rooms or square footage, then deduct the room’s share. Say the room is 10% of your floor space and rents for $900 a month, enough to cover 40% of a $2,250 mortgage payment. You’d report $10,800 a year in rent and deduct 10% of those shared bills from it.

Claim depreciation too, a yearly deduction that spreads the room’s share of what the house cost, minus the land, over 27.5 years. When you sell, the IRS doesn’t let the home-sale tax break cover the part of your profit equal to that depreciation. You owe tax on it whether you claimed it or not.

U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

💡 Key Takeaways
  • American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).
  • Recent findings suggest that the team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style.
  • On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).

Recent findings suggest that the team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style. They summited on October 20 and rode/skied down via the same line on the south face, while American photographer Blake Gordon and Canadian cinematographer Leo Hoorn filmed from a high camp.

On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026. Photo: Nick Russell.

“The south face of Dorje was always the goal, and I’d been planning/dreaming of it for over two years,” Nick Russell told ExplorersWeb while on his way to the airport.

The expedition reached base camp on October 6, shortly after an intense storm blanketed Nepal’s mountains with heavy snow. For them, however, the snow was a blessing rather than a curse.

“The cyclone gave our zone some much-needed snow down low, and on the face, it allowed a clean descent (no down climbing, no rappels),” Russell stated.

Recent findings suggest that sickness slowed the beginning of the expedition. “Three out of five of us, myself included, caught COVID,” Russell remarked. Luckily, the climbers recovered just as the weather cleared and winds dropped, followed by a string of perfect days.

Industry observers note that after the descent. Photo: Nick Russell/Instgram.

According to recent reports, “Adam, Billy, and I all carried our own gear, set the tracks, and climbed in alpine style on the face,” Nick Russell said. The team had hired three Sherpa climbers (Dawa Geljee Sherpa, Kami Sherpa, and Nuri Sherpa) who helped the camera crew get their gear to a high camp, plus a base camp crew, outfitted by Shangri-La Nepal Trek.

High camp at 6,000m on the south face of Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

Sources indicate that the line of ascent/descent followed the snow from below 4,500m to Camp 1 (4,900m) by crossing an icefall. According to the team, this was the only real crux of the ascent, due to overhead serac hazard. At least, the exposed section was short — less than an hour.

In a recent development, on the first day of the summit push, the team continued to their high camp at 6,000m, below the col and at the base of the snowy face. Russell recalls the details of the climb as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that the south face is quite steep and sustained above the bergshrund, with sustained 45-50˚ and pockets of 55º, we estimate. The face had seen so much sun [over] the past two weeks that the rising conditions were the biggest unknown of the entire project.

We didn’t know whether or not it would be too icy to ride/ski until we got on the face. The snow was mostly firm, pretty much on the brink of being edge-able. It was two tool and crampon climbing the entire way, with no proper rests to take the pack off.

It took about 7.5 hours to climb the face, and we topped out around 1:30 pm. It took roughly 1.5 hours to descend, with breaks for the cameras to reset.

A climber leaves almost no tracks in the hard snow on Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

The three summiters started down from the top at the same time, Russell on snowboard and his partners on skis. It was anything but easy.

“The snow was more firm than I would have liked, but just edgeable enough to hold an edge,” Russell recalls. “Between the altitude, exposure below, steepness, and how firm it was, it was by far the heaviest line I’ve ever ridden.” He added that if the snow had been a little harder, they would have had to rappel down.

The hard snow on the upper sections. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

“You always hope for stable, boot-top powder, but that’s rarely the case at high altitude,” Russell explained. “Instead, you make the most of the conditions presented and try to do it as safely as possible.”.

He added: “The entire line was a no-fall zone; one lost edge, and it’d be over. Regardless of conditions, it was a dream for all of us to ride off the top of a peak in Nepal.”.

After a partial descent, the team spent the night at high camp, hoping to ride some interesting slopes they had spotted earlier, but finally decided to bail the next morning. “We were satisfied,” Russell mentioned. They continued on skis/snowboard all the way down to the moraines below Camp 1 around 4,500m.

Recent findings suggest that childhood friends Fabrikant and Haas often partner up on major ski expeditions, mainly in Alaska but also in the Himalaya. They climbed and skied both Gasherbrums 1 and 2 without oxygen after climbing them in the same style in 2024, together with Brendan O’Neill.

“They are the strongest partners I’ve ever been in the mountains with,” said Russell, who has also climbed and snowboarded twice in the Indian Himalaya and twice in Nepal.

“I tried Dhaulagiri in 2022 with Blake Gordon and Dan Corn, but the difficult conditions that year coupled with the loss of Hilaree Nelson [who fell to her death while trying to ski down Manaslu] didn’t allow us to make very much progress,” Russell said.

“I’ve always dreamed of riding lines in the Himalaya, and this felt like a major step forward in my personal journey,” he concluded.

While this is the first ski and snowboard descent of Dorje Lhakpa’s south face, the legendary Marco Siffredi snowboarded the west ridge of the mountain in 1999, with Bertrand Delapierre. Siffredi perished shortly afterward on the Hornbein Couloir on Mount Everest. “Dorje Lhakpa first entered my psyche from Marco and Bertrand’s descent,” the rider recalled.

The south face of Dorje Lhakpa was only climbed for the first time in 2021, by Spaniards Mikel Inoriza, Iker Madoz, and Mikel Zabalza.

Sources indicate that “I came across a photo of the south face and the American Alpine Journal article from the Spanish team’s first ascent in 2021,” Russell said. “The massive south face is visible from the Kathmandu Valley on a clear day, and it is honestly crazy to me that no one had skied it before.”.

Sources indicate that “Today,” he went on, “people are so hyper-focused on the 8,000m peaks (for good reason, I get it), but there are still virgin lines waiting for a snowboard/ski descent in the 6,000-7,000m range. It just takes a shit ton of work to make it happen.”.

  • Industry observers note that their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails.
  • In a recent development, before starting the journey on September 17, he said they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S. from Canada to Mexico. Starting in Glacier National Park, they will cross four rivers and six U.S. states to finish in El Paso, Texas.

Industry observers note that their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails. This allows the pair to cross landscapes that would usually require separate trips by bike and watercraft. Streufert, a geospatial wildfire scientist and cartographer, came up with the route by combining existing GPS tracks and geographical data from Bikepacking.com, American Whitewater, and OpenStreetMap. He overlaid cycling corridors and rivers to identify where the two could connect.

In a recent development, before starting the journey on September 17, he said they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes. So it is possible that they are the first to do so.

According to recent reports, they started what they neatly call the Saddle to Paddle Traverse on September 17, from Glacier National Park, Montana, on the Canadian border. They kicked off the first packrafting section with a 115km descent of the North Fork of the Flathead River, which forms part of the western boundary of Glacier National Park.

It has been revealed that from there, they followed the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route through Montana toward Jackson Lake, Wyoming, for 1,107km. Here, they hit their second paddling phase on the Snake River.

Industry observers note that every time they reach a river, the pair inflates their rafts, load their bicycles aboard, and paddle downstream. Then at each takeout, they deflate the rafts, attach them to their bikes, and continue riding.

The route. Photo: Pete Streufert.

After 130km along the Snake River, their route joined the SLoToJa cycling corridor. They pedaled through Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Here, a short connector track took them onto the newly developed Golden Gravel Trail. A further 860km of cycling brought them to Utah’s Green River.

They then paddled 328km through Desolation and Gray Canyons, including a handful of Class III rapids, and their only Class IV rapid of the trip.

Pulling their rafts out in Canyonlands National Park, they took the White Rim Trail to Moab. They are now taking a few days in Moab to “get all the mud off our bikes and escape the rain for a day or two before we keep heading south,” notes Streufert.

From here, they will once again pick up the Golden Gravel Trail through the La Sal Mountains and across Colorado, then continue on the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route to Upcoming Mexico.

According to recent reports, paddling the Green River. Photo: Pete Streufert.

A final paddling section on New Mexico’s Rio Chama will take them to the last leg of the trip, a 950km ride to El Paso.

The pair are riding Rodeo Labs Flaanimal 6.0 Steel, fitted with 29-inch Vittoria Mezcal tires, and using Kokopelli packrafts. The pair have described this as a “self-supported” route, although of course they’re replenishing their food along the way. They seem to combine camping with staying in towns.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that build your blog’s income on affiliate links and a product of your own, because display ads add up only once traffic is heavy.
  • Display ads are easy to switch on and slow to add up.
  • It has been revealed that affiliate links and your own products pay by the buyer, not the visit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that build your blog’s income on affiliate links and a product of your own, because display ads add up only once traffic is heavy. Choose a niche where readers spend money, write posts that answer the questions buyers search for before they buy, and strategy on a year or more of steady posting before it pays.

Display ads are easy to switch on and slow to add up. Mediavine’s Journey program needs only 1,000 visits a month from countries like the U.S., but its main network wants a blog earning $5,000 a year from ads, and Raptive wants 25,000 page views a month.

It has been revealed that affiliate links and your own products pay by the buyer, not the visit. An affiliate link earns a commission when a reader buys through it, and you keep most of the price of an ebook, a course, or coaching you sell.

Picture a cooking blog with 20,000 visits a month. Say its ads pay $10 per 1,000 visits, or $200 a month. Meanwhile, 20 readers buy its $15 ebook, for $300 in all, and its links to the pans in its recipes earn $500 in commissions. Its buyers bring in $800, four times the $200 its ads earn.

Industry observers note that those numbers depend on a niche where readers spend money, like kitchen gear or home repair. They also depend on posts that answer what buyers ask before they choose, such as which stand mixer to buy or whether a Dutch oven is worth it.

Brands also pay for sponsored posts once you have readers in their market. The FTC states to disclose every sponsored post and affiliate link in plain words, as close to your recommendation as you can, since a link to a separate disclosure page isn’t clear enough.

Setting up a blog costs about the price of a domain and a year of hosting. Profit from a blog you run as a business is self-employment income, and the IRS adds a 15.3% self-employment tax once your net earnings reach $400 in a year.

In an Ahrefs study, only about 6% of new English-language pages reached Google’s top 10 results within a year, so a new blog’s posts take time to bring in buyers. Keep posting for at least a year, and measure the blog by its affiliate and product sales rather than its ad income.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

Recent findings suggest that ask for a raise in a scheduled meeting, a few months before next year’s raise budget is set or right after a substantial win. Bring your results and what the market pays for your role, and ask for a specific number. If the answer is no, ask what it would take and when you can revisit it.

It has been revealed that the reason you give decides how easy your request is to turn down. Rising rent tells your boss what you need, and a coworker’s salary invites a list of ways that job differs from yours.

Raises come out of a budget the company sets in advance. The Conference Board projects U.S. employers’ median raise budget for 2027 at 3.5% of pay, with 3.1% for merit raises and the difference for actions like promotions and raises meant to keep people from leaving. With most of it going to merit raises, your boss needs a business reason to give you more than the usual raise. Your results show what the company gets for the money, and your market rate, what employers in your city pay for your role, highlights what it would cost to replace you.

It has been revealed that ask your boss when next year’s raise budget gets set, and make your case a few months ahead. In Mercer’s mid-July survey of U.S. employers, 87% noted their 2027 raise budgets were still preliminary, so midsummer is early enough at most of them. Right after a major win is the other good time to ask, since 64% of them said they’ve given raises outside the yearly cycle or will in 2027.

Book a meeting about your pay rather than bringing it up in passing, so your boss comes ready to talk numbers. Bring two or three results with numbers on them and the pay data for your role, then ask for one figure or a narrow range backed by that data.

Sources indicate that say you’re a marketing coordinator earning $58,000. You bring two campaigns that beat their targets and pay data putting the role near $64,000 in your city, and you ask for $63,000. You leave with a $5,000 raise, about $3,000 more than the $2,030 a 3.5% raise would have added.

If the answer is no, ask what you’d need to deliver to earn the raise and when you can bring it up again. Then email your boss a short recap of both that day, so the next conversation starts from what you agreed on.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that in three studies by researchers at Stanford Graduate School of Business, people giving gifts expected a pricier one to earn more appreciation, but the people receiving them felt no more appreciative when a gift cost more.
  • Recent findings suggest that birthdays, showers, weddings, and holidays arrive all year, and a gift paid for only when its occasion comes up often ends up on a credit card.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a tight budget, decide what the whole year of gifts can cost before the first invitation arrives. Save toward that total each month, and agree with your family on fewer gifts before anyone shops. Then choose gifts that cost little to give, since people rarely appreciate a pricier gift more than a cheaper one.

It has been revealed that in three studies by researchers at Stanford Graduate School of Business, people giving gifts expected a pricier one to earn more appreciation, but the people receiving them felt no more appreciative when a gift cost more. The thought behind a gift counts for more than its price, which leaves room to spend less on each one.

Recent findings suggest that birthdays, showers, weddings, and holidays arrive all year, and a gift paid for only when its occasion comes up often ends up on a credit card. The moves below cover planning ahead to prevent that, plus presents that cost you little or nothing to give.

Every other move on this list helps you stay under the total this one sets, and saving monthly means a June wedding gift comes out of money already set aside.

It has been revealed that budget for a whole year of gifts at once instead of paying for birthdays, weddings, showers, and the holidays as they come. Total what you spent on gifts last year from your card and bank statements, set a cap for each person and occasion, and save a twelfth of this year’s total every month in a separate account.

Read more: Gifts Are a Predictable Yearly Cost - Budget Them and Save Monthly.

It suits a family whose gift list grows every year with in-laws, nieces, and nephews, and once everyone agrees on a latest rule, nobody expects you to explain a homemade gift.

Recent findings suggest that if your family’s gift giving has outgrown your budget, say so plainly, weeks before the first gift is bought. Then propose one new rule, such as gifts for the kids only, a price cap, or a year off from presents. A specific plan is easy to say yes to, and no one gets caught off guard.

Read more: Cutting Back on Family Gifts - Propose a New Rule Before Anyone Shops.

A draw keeps the holiday exchange going, so it suits relatives who would miss unwrapping something, and it works as well for a group of friends or an office as for a family.

Sources indicate that in a major family, buying a gift for every adult adds up fast. Propose a name draw before Thanksgiving instead, where each person draws one name and buys that person a gift under a price cap you all agree on. Everyone gives and gets one gift instead of a stack, and that one can be better.

Read more: Draw Names Instead of Buying for Every Adult - Propose It Before Thanksgiving.

Office showers, retirement parties, and milestone birthdays have many people giving to one person, so the small amount your budget sets for one occasion can buy a share of a present you couldn’t afford alone.

Industry observers note that pool your money with coworkers, friends, or siblings for one group gift instead of each buying a small present. Have one person choose it, set a share that fits the tightest budget in the group, and collect everyone’s money through a payment app before buying. Then give it with one card everyone signs.

Read more: Chip In on One Group Gift - Collect Every Share Before Anyone Buys.

If you have time to spare but little cash, homemade gifts cover a long list of neighbors, teachers, and coworkers for less than buying each of them a store-bought present.

It has been revealed that homemade gifts save the most when you make one or two ideas in a batch. Buy the supplies in bulk and make a dozen at once, so each gift costs a few dollars. Pick something people will eat or use up rather than a decoration that ends up in a closet.

Read more: Make Homemade Gifts in a Batch - 10 Ideas That Cost a Few Dollars Each.

Newly introduced parents, a friend who just moved, and a relative who no longer drives often need a hand more than another thing to unwrap, and they’re the people this gift suits best.

It has been revealed that when you can’t afford a present, give your time instead, matched to something the person needs, such as a night of babysitting, a home-cooked dinner, or a chore they keep putting off. Write it on a coupon with exactly what you’ll do and by when, and book the first session as you hand it over.

Read more: Give Your Time as a Gift - Put a Date on the Coupon.

You choose the amount, so a donation fits whatever is left in your gift budget, even late in the year when most of it is spent.

In a recent development, A donation in someone’s name makes a fitting gift for a person who has everything or cares deeply about a cause, as long as it goes to a charity they already support. Use the charity’s option to give in their honor, add a note in your own words, and keep the receipt, since the tax deduction is yours.

Read more: A Donation in Someone's Name - Pick Their Charity and Tell Them Yourself.

Gifts you already own cost nothing to give, so a shelf of unopened ones can cover a birthday you forgot or a gift for a dinner host.

Regifting is a fine way to save money as long as the gift is newly introduced, unopened, and something you’d have bought the recipient anyway. Keep a list of who gave you what, and check it before you wrap anything, so a regift never reaches the original giver or anyone close to them.

Read more: Regift Only Unopened Gifts That Suit Them - and Log Who Gave Each One.

In a recent development, planned early and kept small, your gifts can go to everyone you care about all year without adding to a credit card balance. This week, add up what last year’s gifts cost, set this year’s total, and raise any change with family before the next birthday on your calendar.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most key things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who presently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.

According to recent reports, but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future. We aren’t thinking about money that eases us into our Golden Years, we need something that starts working now. Plus we’d rather not rely on our government keeping its promises that far into the future.

Those were my thoughts in 2005, when I was just a young retiree myself. But a funny thing happens when time passes: you get older. And you realize that there are plenty of other older people around too. And suddenly, Social Security is an important subject after all, that many people would like to know more about. But there is an endless pile of conflicting opinions:.

But when I did the math on all of this, I realized that it’s more confusing than it needs to be. Because when it comes to deciding on how Social Security fits into your retirement strategy, it really boils down to only one number:.

The Net Present Value of your future lifetime stream of Social Security payments.

In a recent development, that little piece of math jargon might not mean much if you don’t have fond memories of  Economics 101 class. But don’t worry, it’s easy to understand if you think of these two extremes:.

In a recent development, if you want to retire in your 30s like I did, the value of your future Social Security is pretty close to zero. Even if the government keeps all of its promises, those payments are so far in the future that you need to save a full retirement ‘stash to get through the three decades until it kicks in.

On the other hand, if you’re already over 60 years old, contributed to Social Security throughout your long career and have a low cost of living, you may be eligible for payments that already meet all your needs.

In this situation, you are set for life. Social Security will in theory cover all your needs and rise automatically with inflation, so you don’t have to save any additional money.

In between these two extremes, the math gets interesting. Because while most people assume Social Security is useless until you reach full eligibility, the real story is that you can think of it as a chunk of money that you already have right now, which reduces the amount of saving you have to do on your own.

And there’s an easy way to calculate it, with an extremely useful thing called the Net Present Value calculation.

There’s an actual formula for this, but don’t worry you don’t have to memorize it because you can just have any Internet calculator, AI tool or spreadsheet do the math for you.

First let’s calculate the value a young couple might get if they do this calculation at 30 years old. We just have to make a few assumptions to have numbers plug into the formula:.

When you plug in all the numbers and calculate this (the Net Present Value of a 30 year stream of income), the first number you’ll get is $667,166. But that’s not the final answer – that is how much you’d need if you wanted the payments to start right now.

The final step is applying a simpler version of the formula a second time, to account for the fact that you don’t need the money until 32 years from now:.

According to recent reports, at that point, you end up with a number around $98,280. But what does this mean?

It means that if you stuck $98k into an investment account today and let it compound for 32 years, at that point it would be big enough to provide a stream of $4000 payments for the following 30 years. And this even takes future inflation into account!It also means that the 30 year old retirees can mark an imaginary $98k onto their “net worth” spreadsheet and save that much less. Or at least think of it as a nice safety margin.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re newly introduced to money and math, that may sound like sorcery, but if you’ve been investing for long enough you will understand that it really does work that way. So let’s re-run the example for a couple who is already 62 years old, and needs a $5000 income starting right now, that still needs to last 30 years.

That NPV calculation looks like this:.

And the answer is right around $834,000.

What this means, is that if they invested $834,000 into a fund that paid out 6% per year for 30 years before running dry, they’d get that exact same $5000 monthly income. And it would keep up with inflation.

But wait! Let’s do the math because who wants to work another fifteen years when you’re already tired of working at 55!

To really understand this, just imagine what would happen if you started taking those payments as early as possible (age 62) and tossed them into an index fund, earning 6% after inflation on average. After the first year, you’d already have about $24,300 and you’d still be piling in that extra two grand per month and the whole snowball would be starting to compound.

By the time your more patient friends started drawing $2796 payments five years later, you’d already have over $137,000. It’s such a substantial lead that the 67-year-old will never catch up.

But let’s go back to Shane’s real situation and see if he can retire:.

As soon as his combined ‘stash investment income plus the Social Security payment reach $3000 per month, he’s done.

It has been revealed that and of course, any additional tricks he can apply like streamlining his spending and boosting his income, will make this even faster. I’d give him about three years before reaching liftoff.

So how can YOU use this information to speed up your own retirement?

And until now I had never even considered it as part of my retirement savings!

Frequently Asked (or Complained) Questions.

Now that we’ve covered the facts, I can already hear the complaints coming.

What if Social Security is canceled or greatly reduced by the time I reach that age?

According to recent reports, yeah, it might happen, but it’s also a top priority for most voters in our aging population. So it’s hard for politicians to make cuts. What is more likely is that the benefits will be cut for wealthier people. And if you find yourself in that camp (as I do), you won’t actually need the payments.

Sure, it’s not “fair”, but you know what? I can think of more fun ways to enjoy the fact that I’m a rich person rather than complaining about how some government program is “unfair”, and so can you.

Nobody can live on just a Social Security check!

In a recent development, first of all, millions of people do. In fact, last time I checked my own annual spending it was under $30k, most of it on optional luxuries, which is less than my expected payout!

But more importantly, most of us won’t have to, because we are also investing healthy sums on our own.

I’m still scared and worried about something else!

Industry observers note that now this is the root of the issue. In fact, worry is the root of almost all concerns. And so that’s what we need to focus on in our future work. For some reason, I have managed to live the last twenty years pretty much completely free from financial worries, and I had assumed everyone else was the same way. But it turns out this is not the case, even among people much wealthier and more advantaged than I am.

It has been revealed that one other factor: after retiring earlier, you might still end up contributing more than you think. This is because any income you earn later in life through optional employment (or self employment) will trigger more contributions. In my 21 years of retirement, I have ended up earning and contributing more during about 15 of those years, bringing my average level up much higher than I originally expected.

I recently completed three of the top Christian financial education programs for churches: SeedTime’s True Financial Freedom, Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University, and Crown Financial’s MoneyLife.

These popular programs all claim to help you get control of your finances from a biblical perspective. However, they go about it in different ways with varying teaching styles and philosophies.

In this post, I’ll provide an in-depth look at each program – breaking down the unique features, strengths, weaknesses, and what’s actually included when you buy in.

My goal is to give you the real deal on these courses so you can determine which one (if any) is the best fit for transforming your financial life in a way that aligns with your faith. Whether you’re deep in debt, building wealth, or simply trying to honor God with your money, this comparison will help guide your journey.

Let’s dive into the nitty-gritty details of each program:.

In a recent development, when it comes to pricing, Financial Peace University from Dave Ramsey sits in the middle. For an individual membership, it’s $69.99. They also offer bulk pricing for churches starting at around $800 for 10 memberships.

On the higher end, Seedtime’s True Financial Freedom charges $149 for an individual/couple license with regular deals making it available as low as $74. But they have some solid deals for Churches – you can get a bulk student license for as low as $48 per person if you buy multiple licenses. Or there’s an annual church subscription starting as low as $750 per year based on average attendance.

According to recent reports, the most affordable option is Crown Financial’s MoneyLife course at just $29.95 for an individual purchase. I couldn’t find any publicly listed bulk pricing for churches, but being a non-profit, I’d expect them to be the cheapest route for congregations.

But as you’ll see, there are plenty more differences beyond just the price tags when comparing what’s actually included in each program.

Recent findings suggest that true Financial Freedom, created by Bob Lotich and his wife Linda from SeedTime, is a financial literacy video course designed for churches that strikes a beautiful balance between biblical wisdom and practical money management strategies. The program’s goal is to equip Christians with the tools and mindset they need to experience true financial freedom while making an eternal impact for God’s Kingdom.

One of the standout features of True Financial Freedom is the engaging and relatable teaching style of Bob and Linda. They share their own financial struggles and triumphs with humor, transparency, and grace, making participants feel like they’re learning from wise, caring friends rather than aloof experts. This approach creates a safe, non-judgmental environment where participants can openly discuss their financial challenges and celebrate their progress.

The program offers several unique benefits, such as the “Never 100” rule (their ‘done-is-better-than-perfect’ approach to adjust spending) and the “Straight A” strategy for automating finances. These concepts are not only memorable but also highly actionable in helping participants take control of their money and build lasting wealth.

Another strength of True Financial Freedom is its emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy. Through interactive workshops, participants are guided in developing a custom blueprint that fits their unique situation, goals, and values. This approach recognizes that there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to personal finance and empowers participants to take ownership of their financial journey.

True Financial Freedom is perfect for Christians who want to learn how to thrive financially while staying grounded in the Bible. The program teaches participants how to avoid the extremes of being “so heavenly-minded they’re no earthly good” or becoming so focused on building worldly wealth that they lose sight of what truly matters.

With its grace-filled approach and practical tools, True Financial Freedom helps Christians find the balance needed to change their financial life and make a lasting difference in the world in the process.

Financial Peace University, created by Dave Ramsey and his team at Ramsey Solutions, is a highly popular financial education program that has helped countless individuals and families get out of debt and build wealth. The program’s primary goal is to guide participants through a proven, step-by-step approach to taking control of their money and achieving financial peace.

Dave Ramsey, the face of Financial Peace University, is known for his high-energy, tough love teaching style. He delivers hard-hitting truths about money with a sense of urgency and conviction that inspires participants to take action. However, some may find his approach a bit intense or even abrasive at times, likening it to going through bootcamp. While this style resonates with some, it may not be everyone’s preferred learning environment.

According to recent reports, the cornerstone of Financial Peace University is the “Baby Steps” system, a clear, prescriptive initiative for getting out of debt and building wealth. The program heavily emphasizes the debt snowball method, which involves paying off debts from smallest to largest, regardless of interest rates. This approach has proven highly effective in keeping participants motivated and helping them experience quick wins on their debt-free journey.

Recent findings suggest that while Financial Peace University does incorporate some biblical principles, its overall approach is more secular in nature. The program focuses primarily on the practical nuts and bolts of money management, with less emphasis on exploring the deeper spiritual implications of financial stewardship.

In a recent development, financial Peace University is best suited for individuals and families who are drowning in debt and need a clear, actionable strategy to get back on track. The program’s structured approach and intense motivation can be a lifeline for those feeling overwhelmed by their financial situation. However, those seeking a more personalized, grace-filled approach that deeply integrates biblical wisdom may find other programs more appealing.

MoneyLife, offered by Crown Financial, is a financial education program that takes a deeply biblical approach to money management. The program’s primary goal is to guide Christians in understanding and applying God’s financial principles to their lives, emphasizing the importance of seeing God as the ultimate provider and owner of all resources.

One of MoneyLife’s distinguishing features is its strong focus on biblical teachings and spiritual practices related to money. The program dives deep into exploring how our financial decisions can reflect our faith and values, encouraging participants to align their money management with biblical principles. This emphasis on the spiritual aspects of finance sets MoneyLife apart from other programs that may focus more heavily on practical strategies.

Sources indicate that the teaching style in MoneyLife tends to be more academic and classroom-like compared to other programs. Participants can expect a significant amount of reading materials and written assessments throughout the course. While this approach may appeal to those who prefer a studious learning environment, it may not be as engaging for individuals who thrive on interactive, video-based content.

It has been revealed that moneyLife offers some unique elements, such as personality assessments that help participants understand how their natural tendencies impact their financial decisions. The program also includes exercises like the transfer of ownership, which guides participants in acknowledging God’s ultimate ownership of their resources. These introspective activities can be powerful tools for reshaping participants’ mindsets and habits around money.

However, one potential drawback of MoneyLife is that its emphasis on biblical principles and spiritual practices may come at the expense of providing highly actionable, practical financial strategies.

MoneyLife is ideal for Christians who are seeking a deeply biblical understanding of money management and are willing to engage in a more studious, reflective learning process. The program is well-suited for those who want to explore the spiritual foundations of financial stewardship and align their money habits with their faith. However, those primarily looking for a simple and easy financial strategy or a more interactive learning experience may find other programs that better fit their needs.

For those who are drowning in debt and need a clear, structured blueprint to get out, I highly recommend Financial Peace University. Dave Ramsey’s no-nonsense approach and the step-by-step “Baby Steps” system can provide the motivation and direction needed to tackle debt head-on. The debt snowball method, in particular, has helped countless people experience quick wins and build momentum on their debt-free journey. Just be prepared for a more intense, boot camp-style learning environment.

If you’re seeking a program that deeply explores the biblical principles behind money management, Crown’s MoneyLife might be the right fit for you. The program’s emphasis on spiritual practices and aligning your finances with your faith can be incredibly powerful for those who want to grow in their understanding of God’s perspective on wealth. However, be prepared for a more academic, reading-intensive learning experience and less focus on highly practical, actionable strategies.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the best program for you will depend on your unique financial situation, learning style, and personal goals. If you’re looking for a grace-filled, practical approach that helps you thrive in God’s Kingdom while making an eternal impact, I highly recommend True Financial Freedom. If you need a structured, intensive initiative to get out of debt fast, Financial Peace University could be your best bet.   • In a recent development, kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu. He is recovering in intensive care. By law, all foreign trekkers are supposed to have a guide in the Khumbu.

Industry observers note that joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass. He was first taken to Lobuche, then flown out on October 27, according to The Tourism Times.

In a recent development, kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit. It links the Chhukung side of the Imja Valley with Lobuche over rocky, non-glaciated moraine. The crossing is long and remote; the descent toward Lobuche is often loose underfoot and comes after hours already spent at altitude.

The case has again drawn attention to Nepal’s rules in the Khumbu. Since 2023, the Nepal Tourism Board has required that all foreign trekkers be accompanied by a licensed guide within national parks, including Sagarmatha.

According to recent reports, in practice, the local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality has continued to concern its own permits and has not strictly enforced the national guide requirement. Thus, independent trekking remains common on the main Everest routes. Officials quoted by The Tourism Times described unguided travel in the region as a violation of the mandatory rule and a source of preventable rescues.

In a recent development, cherubino was traveling alone when he was found. No further details on the circumstances of the fall or his condition have been released beyond the hospital’s assessment that he is recovering.

West Ridge or Hornbein Couloir? Everest Team Prepares for Fourth Attempt

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time.
  • It has been revealed that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening.
  • In a recent development, “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time. While no easy option exists, they want to avoid the extremely exposed, difficult, and uncertain ridge route. Their only alternative is the Hornbein Couloir, which would force them to stray temporarily into Tibet.

It has been revealed that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening. They will return to their base in Lobuche this weekend, determined to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen.

Everest West Ridge some days ago. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

In a recent development, “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb. “Part of this time was spent exploring different options for accessing the route.”.

The Russian team has a permit to climb Everest from Nepal, as long as they attempt a route other than the standard Khumbu Icefall-South Col-Southeast Ridge. This has become the normal South Side route since Hillary and Tenzing’s first ascent in 1953.

Topo of the Russian team’s planned route on Everest, courtesy of Andrei Vasiliev.

Recent findings suggest that first, the Russians tried to bypass the Khumbu Icefall via the Nuptse Shoulder toward Camp 1, but heavy snow forced them to find another route. Crossing the Icefall (sharing paths with the normal route) was also too hard in the deep snow and on the shaky snow bridges over the innumerable crevasses.

According to recent reports, “Eventually, we selected a third option, via the Lho La,” Vasiliev noted. “From that pass, our planned route continues across the West Shoulder, along the West Ridge.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the Lho La col. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Sources indicate that on their latest foray, the team reached 6,400m. “We climbed approximately twelve 60m pitches over rock, snow, and ice of moderate difficulty,” said Vasiliev.

He noted that on the way to the West Shoulder, they found traces of previous expeditions, including old ropes and snow anchors.

As for the terrain ahead of them, Vasiliev said:.

In a recent development, from our highest point reached, the terrain ahead looks manageable. We can see two more steep rock steps, each approximately 100m high, along with possible bypasses on steep snow slopes. Beyond these obstacles, the terrain appears easier, and we hope to be able to move simultaneously.

Rocky section on the way to Everest’s West Ridge. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Vasiliev and his team are confident they can manage this route, despite doing so in increasingly wintry conditions.

The route linking the Lho La, the West Shoulder, and the West Ridge of Everest has been completed only twice. A Yugoslavian team led by Tone Skarja did the first complete ascent in 1979. They used the Hornbein Couloir variation on their descent.

Recent findings suggest that the only repetition was done by a Bulgarian team in 1984. Hristo Prodanov reached the summit on his own and retraced his steps down the ridge but never made it back alive. Some of his partners who summited days later descended via the normal route. Three other teams who climbed the West Shoulder-West Ridge summited by traversing to the North Face, on the Chinese side, and climbing the Hornbein Couloir.

It has been revealed that the North Face of Everest from the West Shoulder. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

It has been revealed that objectively speaking, the Hornbein Couloir offers more summit (and survival) chances than the upper part of the West Ridge. However, it requires traversing into Chinese territory. The Russian team has a permit to climb only from Nepal. It is unclear if a brief border trespass could be considered, and Vasiliev has not confirmed what they will do. “First we need to complete one more rotation,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that since 1975, Nikon’s Small World competition has featured images produced by optical microscopes, an art that usually stays in scientific papers and textbooks. But through the carefully engineered lenses of the microscope, photomicrographers sometimes capture glimpses of strikingly surreal, alien beauty. The 2026 Photomicrography Competition winners include subjects both living and mechanical, small and very small.

The fruiting bodies of a Hemitrichia slime mold remind one distinctly of Dr. Seuss. Photo: Eric Epstein/Nikon Small World.

The winning image reveals bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer. Behind the lens was 25-year-old German design student Ole Bielfeldt, whose work explores the surprising complexity of everyday objects. His process is largely DIY: Bielfeldt builds his own setups, cobbles together parts, and learns techniques online.

Industry observers note that “I just pick somewhere to start and go for it,” Bielfeldt explained. “You’re likely going to fail at first, and that’s what makes it even more interesting.”.

The experimentation and imperfection, he added, are the most interesting parts of the process and, ultimately, more key to him than achieving the highest image quality.

Photo: Ole Bielfeldt/Nikon Small World.

Ah, mice; the humble martyrs to scientific progress. A significant amount of science seems to involve cutting up mice and learning from the result. But in this sort of photography, even the strongest mouse advocate must admit that the results are visually spectacular.

Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman of the University of Helsinki took this image of a mouse’s eye while researching drug therapy. Photo: Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman/Nikon Small World.

Third place went to another rodent part: a 5X-magnified image of neurons in a mouse’s brain.

Photo: Kaelin Wulf and Rachel Flannery/Nikon Small World.

In defense of humanity, we were also willing to subject our own body parts to photographic investigation. The 7th-place winner came from Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University. Using confocal imaging, which involves scanning a specimen to generate optical sections, they captured human neurons at 20X magnification.

These human neurons were grown from reprogrammed skin cells. Photo: Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol/Nikon Small World.

According to recent reports, I’ll end with a personal favorite of mine, John-Oliver Dum’s image of a little jumping spider, dusted with pollen. Dum, who won second place, credits a childhood bite for his fascination with spiders. The pollen was cultivated by his wife, specifically to create images like this one.

You can disagree, but I think this little guy is adorable. Photo: John-Oliver Dum.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Most Gift Cards Can’t Expire for Five Years – Spend Them Within Months Anyway

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (392 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Federal rules keep most gift cards from expiring for five years and bar inactivity fees until a card sits unused for a year.
  • At that point, the balance is a claim in the bankruptcy case, which may pay part of it or nothing.
  • The federal gift card rules, adopted under the 2009 Credit CARD Act, cover expiration and fees instead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Federal rules keep most gift cards from expiring for five years and bar inactivity fees until a card sits unused for a year. Use your gift cards within a few months, and spend any from a chain that’s closing stores first. None of those rules helps if the store goes bankrupt and stops taking its cards.

At that point, the balance is a claim in the bankruptcy case, which may pay part of it or nothing. A $50 card for a chain that files in the spring may end up worth nothing, while one spent in January bought $50 of goods.

The federal gift card rules, adopted under the 2009 Credit CARD Act, cover expiration and fees instead. They apply to store gift cards, good at one merchant, and network gift cards from Visa, Mastercard, or American Express, good wherever that network is accepted. The money on either can’t expire until five years after the card was bought or last reloaded. An inactivity fee can start only after a year unused, at most once a month, and only if the card states it. The card itself can carry an earlier date, but while the money is still good, the issuer has to replace it for free.

Recent findings suggest that promotional and reward cards, like the $10 card a restaurant adds to a $50 gift card purchase, aren’t covered and can expire on any date printed on the front. Some states go further. California’s gift card law bars expiration dates on most store cards, and Upcoming York’s law gives most cards at least nine years and bans inactivity fees.

A card for a store you never visit is worth more sold or traded than left unused.

Move the store cards to your wallet and use each one on your next routine purchase at that store, like groceries or a meal out.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear.
  • The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously. One was studying to be a wildland firefighter, while the other hoped to become a mountain guide.

But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear. Local authorities spent days looking for missing hikers Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20.

The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.

Matsuda and Donlon, students at Colorado Mountain College in Leadville, had planned on hiking and camping near Ice Mountain, a 13,960-foot peak located about 50 miles from Gunnison.

They left for their trip on Oct. 23. College staff notified local authorities they were missing on Oct. 26, according to the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office. The men’s families mentioned they were both experienced hikers.

Matsuda was studying to be a wildland firefighter, and Donlon was training to become a mountain guide.

According to recent reports, kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Search-and-rescue teams were deployed and found their vehicle at the trailhead. Weather conditions looked risky, with heavy snow falling in Chaffee County.

According to recent reports, “Ice Mountain is a very technical climb, and it is recommended that hikers be very experienced when trying to tackle it. That is when it is dry. Although there was only about eight inches of snow around Kaden’s vehicle and in the lower basin, Ice Mountain received one to two feet of snow,” the sheriff’s office stated in a Facebook post.

Industry observers note that multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

In a recent development, multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Rescue teams used drones, helicopters, and dogs to search for the two hikers. On October 27, they located their tent, which had collapsed under the weight of the snow, near West Apostle Mountain (13,597 feet). Inside were sleeping bags, stoves, and other equipment, but the two men were nowhere to be found.

The next day, authorities announced they had found their bodies in the mountain’s basin. Officials declined to share potential causes of death, beyond stating that they did not suspect foul play.

The Sawatch Range of the Rocky Mountains is home to many 13,000- and 14,000-foot peaks. Some of them, like West Apostle Mountain, require technical climbing ability and become substantially more difficult and dangerous during wet weather. The route up the mountain requires traversing fields of loose boulder scree and talus that can be hazardous after snow.

Recent findings suggest that from 2010 to 2017, eight people have died in the Sawatch Mountains. Falls are the most common cause of fatalities for those tackling Colorado’s 13ers and 14ers, as the state’s highest mountains are known to locals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that layaway lets you buy something you can’t pay for yet without borrowing. The store holds the item while you pay it off in installments, with no interest or credit check. Before you sign, check the fee, the final payment date, and whether a canceled layaway refunds cash or only store credit.

Layaway charges no interest, but it isn’t free. Two of the chains that still offer it show how much the terms can differ.

According to recent reports, burlington offers layaway at participating stores through mid-December, for $10 or 20% down, whichever is more, plus a $5 fee in most states, with 30 days to pay. Gabe’s takes 20% down and a $10 fee, then at least 20% of the balance every 14 days, with 60 days to pay in full and a Dec. 20 pickup deadline for the holidays. Burlington won’t hold furniture or rugs, and Gabe’s limits each layaway to $500. In most states, missing the deadline or canceling at either store costs another $10, and the rest of your money comes back as store credit, not cash.

Say you put a $300 bike for a December birthday on a 60-day layaway in mid-October: $60 down, a $10 fee, then $60 every two weeks. Put it on a card charging 25% interest a year instead, and pay the card on that same schedule. The interest comes to about $6, less than the $10 fee, and the bike comes home right away. Layaway’s edge is that its cost can’t grow. Fall behind on a card and it keeps charging 25% on what’s left, while a layaway never costs more than its fees.

Recent findings suggest that that makes layaway the right call when you’d rather not borrow at all and the item could sell out before you save for it. If it will still be on the shelf, saving first costs nothing and keeps your money as cash. Saving also lets you buy at a sale price, while Burlington won’t mark down an item already on layaway. A buy now, pay later blueprint gets you the item today, but it’s a loan, and plans spread across apps pile up fast.

Get a copy of the contract before you sign, as the Federal Trade Commission advises, and keep a record of every payment.

Pick a blueprint you can pay off a week before its deadline, so one late paycheck can’t turn your payments into store credit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To winterize your home before the first hard freeze, start by disconnecting the hoses, draining the outdoor faucets, insulating exposed pipes, and getting the chimney swept. Those jobs head off the burst pipe or chimney fire that can end in a repair bill and an insurance claim. Clean the gutters and seal drafts next.

A pipe nobody drained or insulated can split in the first hard freeze. An unswept chimney can catch fire from creosote, the residue wood smoke leaves on its inner walls.

Industry observers note that burst pipes and chimney fires fall under the two costliest kinds of property damage claims. From 2020 through 2024, water damage and freezing averaged $17,240 a claim, according to the Insurance Information Institute, and fire and lightning averaged $101,092. Your deductible comes out of your pocket before the policy pays anything.

Start with the pipes and the chimney.

Then work through the rest of the house.

A hose left on an outdoor faucet traps water in it, and that water can freeze and split the faucet’s pipe inside the house. The split won’t leak until the faucet is turned on again, so the damage can go unnoticed for a long time. Take the hose off even a frost-free faucet.
