#33025. Pinnacle Sunrise

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1211 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Thetrek ↗ Open Full Page

Pinnacle Sunrise

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1211 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thetrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that let the record show that I was on time, it was the sun that was early.
  • Sources indicate that call me uneducated, but I could have swore that the time of sunrise wasn’t an especially flexible thing.
  • In a recent development, after the sunrise it was time to make my next decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that let the record show that I was on time, it was the sun that was early. The confusion doesn’t end there.

Sources indicate that call me uneducated, but I could have swore that the time of sunrise wasn’t an especially flexible thing. After a long night mostly in my tent, I was up and alert enough a little after 6:00AM. Sunset was scheduled for 6:44AM, give or take. I enjoyed a nice breakfast, started packing up, started filtering my remaining water, and, at precisely 6:40AM, headed back over to The Pinnacle from my nearby camping spot. The walk couldn’t have been more than a minute, but sure enough, Mr. sun was already halfway above the horizon! I checked my phone, 6:41AM. Classic. I mean, its not substantial deal, the best pictures are of the sun cresting the horizon, which I was still able to get from a few different positions on the various rocks jutting out over the valley. Still, I wanted my special morning moment where the sun first peers over the horizon. Today’s sunrise would be a brief event since clouds were out in force. The sun would soon be un-setting as it disappeared into them. It would be back out in a few hours as the clouds were expected to clear completely by noon.

In a recent development, after the sunrise it was time to make my next decision. I could extend today’s hike and head a bit further south to the Windsor Furnace Shelter and take the blue blaze shortcut back north. It would mean I wouldn’t be returning to The Pinnacle in my next hiking stint, but that might be OK since the weather looked cloudy on Wednesday and rainy on Thursday, there might not be much to see. But I also wanted to wrap up the hiking stint and get back to town. I lost track of the decision while packing up my tent and instinctively took the shorter route back the direction I came from. I blame the chilly morning for this choice, I wasn’t about to sign myself up for extra hiking while I was still trying to get warm. By the time I realized which way I was heading I just accepted it, maybe the weather would turn and I’d see something at The Pinnacle anyway.

Progress was swift on the gravel road leading all the way down to Eckville from The Pinnacle. What a thoughtful place for the trail, especially with the surplus of rocks around. In fact, it was too inviting, I managed to steam along the road until I looked up and realized that I was staring at a blue blaze. I knew immediately I was on the trail down to a parking lot and would need to backtrack uphill to rejoin the AT. By the time I was crossing the road in Eckville I had only just finished my water, so I didn’t feel the need to swing by the shelter for more. I had also already stopped to remove my sleeping layers which were helpful to keep me warm during the first hour or so of hiking, but now I’d be heading uphill and soon the temperature would be hitting the mid sixties. Long Johns would not be necessary.

I spotted a buck along the trail just before the climb back up to the ridge that I would be following all the way. Up on the ridge I had a clear view of The Pinnacle. The clouds were in full retreat. It was a little wild to think I’d woke up there this morning. It wasn’t even 10:00AM, I was making serious time. I put my head down and continued my cruise back to the van.

A buck enjoys the warmth of the sun by the trail.

Industry observers note that looking at The Pinnacle. I started there at 7:00AM and made it all the way here in less than 3 hours!

Looking at The Pinnacle from the trail north. I love how the blue sky creates the illusion that there is another mountain ridge behind it.

It has been revealed that despite the occasional rock-induced slowdowns, I couldn’t be stopped today. That is, except at the Thunderhead Lodge where I again found myself taking a blue blaze trail completely by accident. I decided to stick with this one since it was short and I could easily rejoin the AT once I reached route 309. The blue blaze took me straight to the Thunderhead Lodge which was closed, but the “bartender” was apparently still working. I requested a water refill, but the bartender just told me a joke about customers not being about to hold their liquor. I figured this was the way the establishment tells hikers they are closed and set off to rejoin the AT.

The bartender at the Thunderhead Lodge.

I made it all the way back to my van at 2:30PM. I hiked 21.8 miles of Appalachian Trail in 7.5 hours. The miles going the wrong way down the first blue blaze are not included, neither is time spent stopping for bathroom breaks, wardrobe adjustments, pictures etc. It is safe to say that I hiked at 3 miles an hour overall, a very respectable pace especially since there was some uphill and definitely some tricky rock sections to navigate through. That bodes well for my upcoming 4 state challenge attempt which will be quite time crunched and require sustaining a robust pace.

According to recent reports, with plenty of time left in the day I headed to Reading, PA to put some time into my blog before heading back to the trail. I had been coordinating the return of the Z seat with Pebbles and Greasetrap, they are camping near the road so it should be easy to locate them and return the package to its owner tomorrow morning.

View from the trail near the New Tripoli Campsite.

Total: 21.8 miles, 45,770 steps.

The buyer pays the same price as they would otherwise, and your purchase helps to support The Trek's ongoing goal to serve you quality backpacking advice and information. Thanks for your support!

To learn more, please visit the About This Site page.

Industry observers note that I’m See You Tomorrow (SYT), a 30-something hiker who loves hiking just for the thrill of seeing things that most people don’t. I have no problem eating the same things every day and, for me, over-analyzing everything is half the fun (sometimes more). I am new to backpacking but that won’t stop me from taking on an unorthodox hike of the Appalachian Trail in 2026. It’s not quite a yo-yo, but I have aspirations of hiking the entire trail twice in one year. For the rest of the story you’ll just have to start reading my blog!

Thanks for sharing the beautiful sunrise. That’s a freaky bartender. If you were walking in the woods at night and saw that you might start running, keep trucking buddy almost there.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite a forecast of high winds on November 21 and 22, Andrei Vasiliev, Sergey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov have decided to begin a fresh attempt on the West Ridge of Everest on Sunday.
  • The three stubborn Russians will again proceed via the West Ridge without bottled oxygen, support, or any other living soul on the mountain.
  • The forecasts warn of very high winds all weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite a forecast of high winds on November 21 and 22, Andrei Vasiliev, Sergey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov have decided to begin a fresh attempt on the West Ridge of Everest on Sunday.

The three stubborn Russians will again proceed via the West Ridge without bottled oxygen, support, or any other living soul on the mountain.

The forecasts warn of very high winds all weekend. Nevertheless, they will start up on Sunday, November 22, although that is the day with the strongest winds forecast.

It has been revealed that “That day, we will remain low on the mountain and climb to our Camp 1 at 5,600m,” Sergey Kondrashkin wrote. “From there, we will push upward when the weather improves and the winds die down, aiming to descend around November 28.”.

This means the team does not intend to summit quite yet. The goal is to acclimatize by reaching 7,500m and then return to their headquarters in Lobuche.

“The question is, will we manage to complete the summit push within the time frame of our permit, which expires on December 15, and will the weather cooperate?” said Kondrashkin.

According to recent reports, the fall season on Everest usually lasts until the end of November, since December 1 marks the start of Nepal’s winter climbing season. However, the permit dates may have been extended for this team, which is climbing off the normal route.

Once winter settles in, it will be the turn of Jost Kobusch of Germany, who will attempt to solo Everest in winter along the same route the Russians are now attempting.

On their third and latest trip up the mountain so far, the team only reached 6,700m before hurricane-force winds up to 130kph forced them down, according to former team member Natalyia Belyankina. Belyankina had to leave the expedition for health reasons but has stayed in touch with the others.

  • Pinhoti Outdoor Center’s Facebook post highlighting the pending record-setting FKT.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Record-breaking news from the southeast this week. Although the attempt has yet to be verified, it appears the Pinhoti Trail will soon have a upcoming self-supported Fastest Known Time (FKT).

It has been revealed that on November 15, 2026, the Pinhoti Outdoor Center posted about the latest FKT. According to the post, Katie “Raven” Gunvalson covered the 350-mile Pinhoti Trail through Alabama and Georgia in 6 days, 14 hours, and 39 minutes. If verified, this attempt will establish a latest overall self-supported record for the point-to-point route, which includes approximately 50,000 feet of elevation gain.

Pinhoti Outdoor Center’s Facebook post highlighting the pending record-setting FKT.

In a recent development, the previous women’s record was set in 2022 by Liz Derstine, with a time of 7 days, 18 hours, and 22 minutes. The previous men’s record, which also stood as the overall record, was set in 2020 by Willie Thacker, with a time of 6 days, 16 hours, and 7 minutes. Gunvalson’s 2026 effort shaved nearly two hours off Thacker’s record, establishing a new overall time to beat.

Gunvalson is no stranger to record-breaking efforts. She has set FKTs across the US, including the current female self-supported records on the Oregon Coast Trail and the Ouachita Trail. The Pinhoti Trail attempt would be her first overall record, establishing a upcoming benchmark for all competitors.

Sources indicate that fastestKnownTime.com, the official FKT website and record-verification platform, lists the Pinhoti Trail as 335 miles long. However, FarOut and other trail guides list its length at approximately 350 miles. Gunvalson’s tracking GPX file has yet to be published, so her total mileage has not been confirmed. Upcoming records can take several weeks to be verified and published on the website, so additional information should become available in the coming weeks.

According to FastestKnownTime.com’s guidelines, there are three distinct “styles” that indicate varying levels of outside assistance: unsupported, self-supported, and supported.

Recent findings suggest that unsupported means athletes receive no external assistance and must carry everything they need from start to finish. They may only collect water from natural sources.

Self-supported allows a little more flexibility, permitting athletes to accept assistance they can “manage or find along the way.” Self-supported athletes cannot have resources arranged specifically for them, but they can accept assistance available to other trail users, such as trail magic, hostels, and resupplying in town.

Supported efforts allow unlimited outside assistance, “as long as you are entirely self-powered.” For example, an athlete could receive food and water from a support crew but must continue moving under their own power.

Recent findings suggest that gunvalson’s Pinhoti attempt falls into the self-supported category. So far, there has been little coverage of the achievement, and details about her approach remain unclear. Did she resupply along the way? Did she stay overnight at a hostel? These logistical questions and others will likely be answered once the record is submitted and verified.

In addition to a GPX file, many athletes upload photos and commentary documenting their FKT attempts. In her previous records, Gunvalson has included daily mileage breakdowns, which readers may also be able to look forward to once this attempt is approved and published.

According to recent reports, photo of Katie “Raven” Gunvalson along the Pinhoti Trail. Photo from Pinhoti Trail Alliance’s Instagram.

The Pinhoti Trail was designated a National Recreation Trail in 1977. It spans approximately 350 miles from its southern terminus at Flagg Mountain in Alabama to its northern terminus in Georgia, where it connects with the Benton MacKaye Trail. Flagg Mountain is considered the southernmost peak of the Appalachian Mountain range and stands more than 1,000 feet above sea level.

The Pinhoti Trail is beloved by thru-hikers, section hikers, and day hikers alike. One of the most iconic thru-hikers in recent years even helped establish a hostel along the trail. M.J. “Nimblewill Nomad” Eberhart became the oldest person to thru-hike the Appalachian Trail in 2021 at age 83. His record was broken this year by 91-year-old Dale “Grey Beard” Sanders.

Nimblewill Nomad, along with friends Lloyd and Tammy Caperton, recently opened the donation-based, “no-frills” Southern Comfort Hiker Hostel in Weogufka, Alabama.

According to recent reports, A handful of adventurous hikers also use the Pinhoti as a connector on a border-to-border route along the East Coast known as the East Coast Trail. This route links the Florida Trail, Pinhoti Trail, Benton MacKaye Trail, Appalachian Trail, and International Appalachian Trail.

Since 2021, hikers and trail enthusiasts have flocked to Alabama for Pinhoti Fest, a festival created to promote and celebrate the trail. The Pinhoti is continuing to gain attention and popularity, and Gunvalson’s potential FKT will bring even more awareness to this southern footpath.

The AT was her first thru hike and the place where she would meet her future husband, Truffles. After completing the AT, the pair moved to east Tennessee to work as backpacking guides in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Between guiding gigs, Magic hiked the Arizona Trail in 2023, the West Highland Way in 2024, and the Pacific Crest Trail in 2025. Jost Kobusch to Train For Everest on Difficult, Dangerous Lhotse Shar

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that jost Kobusch of Germany has moved to the Khumbu Valley to finish his acclimatization before attempting to solo winter Everest, beginning on December 22.
  • Sources indicate that kobusch is now in Chukhung village, from which he climbed 6,165m Island Peak (Imja Tse) yesterday.
  • Kobusch’s climb on Island Peak as shown in his tracker today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that jost Kobusch of Germany has moved to the Khumbu Valley to finish his acclimatization before attempting to solo winter Everest, beginning on December 22. His preparations include reaching 8,000m on a different peak.

Sources indicate that kobusch is now in Chukhung village, from which he climbed 6,165m Island Peak (Imja Tse) yesterday. He spent the night at 6,000m, topped out again today, and went back down, as shown in his live tracker. He told ExplorersWeb that he will now rest for a few days in Lukla and then hike up the valley again to inspect conditions on his next acclimatization goal: the difficult Lhotse Shar (8,383m).

Kobusch’s climb on Island Peak as shown in his tracker today.

“My strategy is not to summit but to tag 8,000m up its flank, before heading for Everest,” he said.

Lhotse Shar is one of the main points of the Lhotse ridge, and it is climbed from south side of the mountain, with Chukhung as the starting point. The main options are to climb the southeastern flank of the Shar itself or try a direct line up the formidable south face of Lhotse.

According to recent reports, neither of them is easy, and the upper sections are statistically dangerous. According to Wikipedia, Lhotse Shar has the highest fatality rate of all principal or secondary 8,000m peaks. For every two climbers who summit, one person dies attempting to.

Lhotse and its various points, as seen from the south. Graphic by Gorskie Mapy.

The Austrian expedition that first reached the summit of Lhotse Shar (from the Southeast Ridge) in 1970 set four altitude camps, the uppermost at 7,600m. They used supplemental oxygen on their summit push. “Almost the whole of the route from below Camp 1 to Camp 3 was fixed with rope, as climbing was very difficult,” they reported in the AAJ.

It has been revealed that kobusch will not have to deal with the nearly vertical terrain and cornices near the summit, but will have to face difficult mixed terrain and uncertain conditions if he wants to venture up to 8,000m. He will not use bottled oxygen, and as far as we know, he will climb on his own.

Kobusch plans to reach the base of Everest on December 22 and solo the mountain in winter without oxygen, via the West Ridge — the same line currently being attempted by a Russian team.

It has been revealed that this is Kobusch’s fourth attempt, and he is willing to try to reach the summit this time. However, when asked about it, he admits he does not know if such a feat is actually possible. “Every expedition, every training session, every difficult decision has been part of preparing myself for what I know will be the biggest challenge of my life,” he admits.

Kobusch’s is not the only confirmed climb this winter. Denis Urubko of Russia is reportedly preparing to climb Broad Peak in winter, possibly starting at the end of this year and continuing through January and February. On social media, Urubko mentioned he will be climbing with Vitaliy Skel. However, details of his route have not been confirmed.

It has been revealed that simone Moro of Italy has not decided whether to try Manaslu again this winter. He told ExplorersWeb he is still considering his looks while observing the “crazy weather this season.” Moro attempted Manaslu in fall to acclimatize and become familiar with the terrain. However, like every other team, he had to call off the attempt due to dangerous conditions following extremely heavy snowfall. Moro wants to climb the peak in alpine style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are lower today, but recent averages above 7% are still eating into buyers’ budgets.

In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 21 basis points lower than yesterday and 13 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

Industry observers note that the results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

It has been revealed that investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

In a recent development, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.
